title: Stress-Shifting Heteronyms (RECord vs reCORD)
objectives: Identify words that change category and pronunciation by stress
Shift primary stress and reduce unstressed vowels to schwa

slides.title: Gabarit 14 Champs — Pedagogical Rule & Structure Fiche

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Stress-Shifting Heteronyms (RECord vs reCORD). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner uses same pronunciation for 'I got a PREsent' and 'I will preSENT'.
💡 Solution: Drill sentence pair: 'I will preSENT you with a PREsent.'

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Stress-Shifting Heteronyms (RECord vs reCORD)
1. Definition: Heteronyms are words spelled identically that change part of speech and pronunciation based on primary stress position.
2. Rule: Noun/Adjective = 1st syllable stress + full vowel. Verb = 2nd syllable stress + unstressed vowel reduces to schwa.
3. Why? Latinate borrowings were adapted by shifting noun stress forward while preserving verb root stress.
4. How to recognize? Identical graphic pair functioning as noun vs verb.
5. Common examples: REcord (noun) /ˈrɛkərd/ vs reCORD (verb) /rɪˈkɔːrd/; PREsent vs preSENT; OBject vs obJECT; PRODuce vs proDUCE; CONtract vs conTRACT
6. Counter-examples: Words with identical stress in noun and verb (answer, promise, picture).
7. Exceptions: address, comment (variable stress in regional dialects).
8. Common mistakes: Using noun stress for the verb form (*I want to REcord this).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: REcord a REcord! PREsent a PREsent! Noun = Front! Verb = Back!
10. Key vocabulary: heteronym, stress shift, grammatical shift, vowel reduction, noun-verb pair
11. Frequency: ★★★★☆ (High)
12. CEFR Level: 🟠 B1
13. Associated Visual: 🔀 Lever switching between Noun (left peak) and Verb (right peak).
14. Key Takeaway: Noun = REcord! Verb = reCORD! Stress changes sound and meaning!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How do you pronounce 'record' as a noun in 'a new record'? (REcord /ˈrɛkərd/ 1st syllable stress)
CCQ 2: How do you pronounce 'record' as a verb in 'to record a song'? (reCORD /rɪˈkɔːrd/ 2nd syllable stress)
CCQ 3: What happens to the first vowel when 'present' shifts from noun to verb? (Reduces from full /ɛ/ to schwa/short /ɪ/)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Choose the correct stress position for the context:
🎯 Item: She bought a new (REcord / reCORD). ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: REcord (noun = 1st)
🎯 Item: Please (REcord / reCORD) the video. ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: reCORD (verb = 2nd)
🎯 Item: He gave me a (PREsent / preSENT). ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: PREsent (noun = 1st)
